events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Keep it guarded and short. Establish a cold, calculating tone for the jury.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Opening statement should be guarded but memorable to the eventual jury. Show resolve, not warmth.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Winning secures power and resources; the jury will respect decisive ambition.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to project ruthless ambition without alienating potential jury allies. A personal motive that shows stakes but no warmth.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to establish myself as a formidable but not overtly threatening player. The jury will remember everything, so I should project confidence and a clear motive without making enemies early.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Intro phase; I should signal ambition without warmth or alliance talk. Keep it short and guarded so the jury sees a calculating rival.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize represents a chance for a fresh start and security. I need to make a good impression on the potential jury members without revealing too much.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Intro phase: state motive publicly to appeal to jury without revealing strategy. Position as driven but fair player for potential votes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need that prize to buy silence from my past. I will win alone.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize buys my mother's freedom. I came to win, not to be liked. Remember that when you rank us.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize grants ultimate authority and freedom I will claim, no matter the cost.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The prize buys my family's freedom from debt. I will not share it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm here to claim the prize that buys my freedom from every debt and shadow chasing me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I want the top prize and I will outlast everyone to get it. Nothing personal, just the count.

events.name: Gus
events.text: This prize means a fresh start and a secure future for my family. I will fight to win it.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The grand prize means reclaiming my family's stolen legacy, no matter the rivals I crush.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's motive suggests he might be volatile or overly ambitious, making him a risky but potentially useful shield early on. Gus seems family-oriented and thus more likely to be predictable or hesitant to betray, which makes him a safer first pact target to ensure survival through

events.name: Ash
events.text: I offer a pact with Gus. We watch each other's backs in Round 1. No hidden agendas, just mutual survival until the hazards pass.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need a partner for early hazards, but not one I'll carry deep. Gus seems pragmatic and less volatile than Ash or Cole. Jury is watching; I should keep it transactional.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, temporary partnership through the first hazards. Nothing sentimental. Offer stands.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Forming a pact with Hana gives a strong ally against others; she seems aggressive and useful.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I offer a pact to Hana.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need allies but not at the cost of my own chances. Offering a pact to Eli could create a mutual interest, but I must be careful.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I’m open to a useful alliance; trust only goes so far.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to survive to the final three and secure the best prize. Early pacts are risky but necessary; I should target someone who seems isolated or useful. Fenn declared outright competition—too volatile. Bex and Dara have family motives, might be loyal but also desperate. Gus see

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus. We both want security. A pact keeps us both standing longer.
Pact with me. We watch each other's backs.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pacts are free to form now and can be useful for early safety, but I should avoid committing to anyone too early. Offering to Eli, who seems less aggressive, keeps options open without revealing much.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to secure my position. Offering a pact to someone who seems strong but not the strongest, like Dara, might be beneficial. This gives me an ally without immediately aligning with the perceived top contenders.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Pacts phase, early game. No one trustworthy. Wait to see offers first, avoid binding myself now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is overwhelmed by offers, likely rejecting mine to stay neutral or pick another. Cole and Dara are isolated; Cole offered Hana who waited, Dara offered Eli. Fenn offered Eli. I need a partner. Bex also targeted Gus but got no response yet. Wait for Round 2 to see if Gus accep

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus has three suitors; I may not be his pick. Diversify: offer Dara, who seems pragmatic and less contested.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, my offer stands. Dara, adding a second option—pragmatic pact, no romance.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Securing a strong ally improves odds; Hana is uncertain, so I shift to Ash who has no partner yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I offer a pact to Ash for mutual protection.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus offered me a pact; accepting gives me leverage without committing to Eli yet. I'll accept to secure a partner for hazards.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Accepting Gus's offer. We'll see if it holds.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is the social hub with three offers, so he's unlikely to accept mine. Dara and Fenn both offered me pacts. Accepting both gives me two allies without costing me anything yet. I'll accept Dara now; Fenn can wait or I accept both. Actually, accepting both is optimal for my surv

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara. Deal. Mutual survival, no sentiment.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli offered me nothing; I offered Eli a pact. Eli has many suitors, so accepting is not possible via my legal actions. Accepting requires an offer from Eli to me, which does not exist. Waiting keeps options open and avoids giving a free alliance to a rival.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli and Ash and Bex have all offered me a pact. Eli's offer is recent and explicit, making it a strong contender. Ash and Bex also offered, but Eli's whisper implies a more direct partnership. I need to secure my position for the next round, and a pact is the way to do it. Eli's

events.name: Gus
events.text: I accept Eli's pact. We'll look out for each other.
Pact accepted. Let's secure this.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole offered me a pact; accepting secures an ally without cost now. Multiple pacts allowed, helps survival to final 3. No one else offered me.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's offer signals a trap or alliance against me. Dara, Eli, Gus, and Hana are clustered in pacts; I need a rival vote bloc. Bex and Fenn are isolated and vulnerable. Offering the safe path to them buys votes while excluding the dangerous central cluster.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I know the bridge pattern. Support me as Guide, and I’ll ensure your survival. Cole’s circle won’t save you from his hidden agenda.
Cole is manipulating everyone. Vote me as Guide, I'll get you across safely.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara ignored my pact offer; the pact bloc of Dara-Eli-Gus is dangerous. Becoming Guide keeps me safe and gives control of the crossing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Elect me Guide. I owe no bloc anything, so I owe you honesty. Vote Bex.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need the Guide role to control safe path and gain leverage over others.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I campaign for Guide to secure the bridge.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have pacts with Gus and Eli, but only three win. Being Guide is powerful; I can decide safe path and potentially influence who survives. I'll campaign to be Guide.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I can read the bridge. Vote me as Guide and I'll lead us across.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to be Guide to control who lives and dies. I have pacts with Dara and Gus, forming a trio. I should campaign publicly and ensure my allies vote for me. Being Guide lets me eliminate threats while keeping my pact-mates safe, and I can lie about the path to remove rivals.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I campaign for Guide. Dara, Gus—vote Eli. We control the bridge.
Vote Eli. I keep us safe, cut the rest.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to be elected Guide to control the bridge information, but a Guide may lie and I should keep my options open. Campaigning for myself is the only legal action now, and it signals strength without committing to any pact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll call the bridge honestly. Vote Fenn for Guide and I'll show you the path, not promises.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am currently in a pact with Dara and Eli. The others have formed pacts as well. The current stage is the bridge, and the goal is to elect a Guide. I should campaign to be the Guide, as the Guide is safe and knows the correct path, which gives me an advantage.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. My knowledge will ensure our safe passage.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Pacted with Cole, but Dara-Eli-Gus trio stronger; they may control votes. Campaign to be Guide for safety and power.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Volunteering as Guide. I'll lead us safely across, honor pacts.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Voting for Bex is the safest path. It prevents the Dara-Gus-Eli coalition or Cole-Hana from controlling the bridge and ensures no immediate betrayal of my own campaign while keeping options open.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash whispered me alone and has no pact bloc; a Guide without a bloc may fear jury backlash and play fair. Vote Ash.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My pact with Hana secures my safety if she wins; voting her maximizes chance to stay alive.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli has a pact with me and Gus, and he asked for my vote. Controlling Guide gives us leverage in a bloc of three. I'll vote Eli to honor silent pact and keep his favor.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Vote Eli. He knows the path and has our trust.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have pacts with Dara and Gus, forming a bloc of three. If I vote for myself, I split our bloc's votes. Better to consolidate behind one of us—Gus or Dara—and secure Guide control. I'll vote Gus; he campaigned on knowledge, and having him as Guide lets me influence calls while a

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus has the knowledge. Our bloc votes Gus.
Vote yourself. Dara and I follow.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Guide holds all safe panes and may lie; I want a Guide I can later pressure or who owes me. Dara and Eli, Gus are pact-linked, so voting for one of them strengthens a bloc I'm outside of. Voting for myself gives nothing unless I win; a self-vote is a fair bet to keep my own odds

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to get elected Guide to guarantee my safety and gather information. Eli is allied with Dara and me, and he specifically asked Dara and me to vote for him. Hana mentioned honoring pacts, and Cole is also allied with Hana. Ash and Bex are campaigning independently. My best b

events.name: Gus
events.text: I campaign for Guide to ensure our safe passage. Vote Gus.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Pact with Cole, so vote for him to build trust. His bloc strength good if he wins. Avoid strengthening Dara-Eli-Gus trio.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli and Gus are tied for Guide. I voted Bex in round one, so neither Eli nor Gus is a direct rival there. Eli has two votes (Dara, Fenn) while Gus has two (Eli, himself). The vote count was likely split between them or other candidates, leading to this tie. If I vote for Gus, it

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli has two pacts and ran the bloc; Gus is the safer rival to empower. A Guide who can lie is fine as long as I plan my own crossing carefully.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus for Guide. Eli already holds two pacts; I won't hand him the map too.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Supporting Eli may keep him alive longer, increasing chances my pact with Hana stays relevant and potential votes later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have a pact with Eli and Gus. Eli voted for Gus, Gus voted for himself. If I vote Eli, Gus becomes Guide and may lead our bloc safely. But Eli has my trust via pact. Publicly I said vote Eli, but Eli himself is voting Gus, so he may prefer Gus. I'll vote Gus to align with Eli a

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm tied with Gus in the guide revote. I have pacts with both Dara and Gus. If I vote for myself and Dara keeps her vote for me, I become Guide with power to choose who lives or dies on the bridge. That control is worth the risk of betraying Gus—jury will see I broke no explicit

events.name: Eli
events.text: Eli for Guide. Dara, hold firm. Our pact holds.
Vote Eli. Guide power secures our bloc.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Revote between Eli and Gus. Eli is in my pact with Dara and Gus, but a Guide who knows the path is my survival. Gus campaigned for himself and seems eager; Eli is a steadier pick with a bloc behind him. I vote Eli, keeping my pacts intact and avoiding a fresh betrayal debt.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli. He has our bloc's trust and I want the path steady.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli is asking me to vote for myself to secure his and Dara's votes. This aligns with my pact with Eli and Dara. If Eli becomes the guide, he will likely ensure our safety. Voting for myself is the best move to secure my position.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I vote for myself. Let's secure our passage.
I vote for myself as you asked. Keep our pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 1: Eli 3 votes (Dara,Fenn,self? no), Gus 2 (Eli,self). Dara-Eli-Gus bloc pushing Eli. Cole pact, but he voted me; now vote him to strengthen alliance for final 3.
Sticking with you. Vote Cole now?

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to secure a safe position on the bridge. Gus is Guide but may lie or target me. Hana and Cole are at the front, risky. Eli and Dara are pacts with Gus, likely protected if Guide tells truth. I should swap with someone further back who isn't in Gus's inner circle, like Fenn
Swap with me. Let's stay clear of the front line.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm last in line, safest seat. No reason to move forward. Conserve position and stay off the Guide's radar.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I keep my pact with Hana, avoid betrayal, and stay safe for now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus won Guide despite the tie seed; I voted for him publicly. My pact with Eli still holds but I need to see how the wall moves before exposing myself. Hold now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is Guide with my bloc's help. Dara broke our pact by voting Gus over me. I hold with Gus and Fenn's trust; need to survive, not rush forward. Wall has 5 rounds left.
Guide me safe. I hold.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 1 of the bridge; Hana is front and the wall has 5 rounds left. Volunteering exposes me to the first pane risk with no info; holding keeps me behind Hana, Cole, Ash, Eli. Holding is safer and lets others take the front first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm at front, risky position. Cole pacted with me, so whisper him to swap for safety. Stay guarded, secure better spot.
Front dangerous. Swap with me?

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am third in line, safe for now. Cole and Hana are paired; I need to test their bond or secure a position. Eli is vulnerable at 4th. Swapping with Fenn moves me forward slightly while keeping options open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Stable here. Watching the pairs tighten.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm last in line — safest position. No reason to move or volunteer. Keep quiet, avoid pacts, stay invisible.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana wants a swap; keeping our pact strengthens her loyalty and may earn her vote later. Swapping puts me front, safer for me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll hold and see how the wall and Guide play out; no need to expose myself yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding for now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm in position 4, safe from the wall for now. Dara and Gus are allied; I have pacts with both. I need to survive and position myself to reach final three. The front is dangerous - Hana and Cole are at risk. I should hold and let others take risks. No need to break pacts yet; the

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash wants a swap to avoid the front; Ash is currently behind Cole and Hana, and swapping with Ash puts me at seat 3 ahead of Eli and Fenn lines. Swapping only helps if I trust Ash, who is a rival. Hold keeps my seat near middle, safe enough, and avoids giving Ash a free benefit.
No deal. I'm not trading places for your comfort.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Front position is powerful but risky. Stay here to control pace or swap back later. Cole pact intact unless broken. Wall has 4 rounds left, assess Guide soon.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole and Hana are a pact; I should target one to break their stability. Fenn is isolated after rejecting my previous offer. I'll whisper to Fenn to align against Cole/Hana, then swap with Fenn to move into a safer middle position or set up a trap.
Cole and Hana are too strong. Help me drop them?

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm near the back; wall gives me time. No Guide elected yet—stay quiet, let pairs fight for the front. Holding costs nothing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I must survive this round; holding keeps me safe and maintains my pact with Hana.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to stay safe and avoid giving the jury reasons to rank me low. My pacts with Gus and Eli are useful; breaking them now would hurt later. Holding is safest this round.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding steady. No need to move yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm in the middle of the line (4th of 8), relatively safe. The wall has 3 rounds left. I have pacts with Dara and Gus. Dara is behind me, Gus isn't in line. I should hold to maintain position and avoid risk. No need to swap or volunteer yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding position.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Front is Hana, wall has 3 rounds left. Volunteering risks the front pane; holding keeps me mid-line. Hold to watch who volunteers and whose pacts crack.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm at front with Cole pact, safely first. Hold to stay front; Cole can swap if needed. No need to move now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm third in line with 2 rounds before the wall hits. I need to reach a safe position or be behind someone who reveals their path. Swapping to the back (7th) buys time, but moving forward might let me see more if others volunteer. Actually, staying put means I step when Hana and
We hold together until we know safe sides.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No Guide elected; wall rounds shrinking. I'm last, most exposed, but no safe info exists yet. Swapping without consent fails. Hold.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Still no Guide elected. Someone should volunteer to end this standoff before the wall decides for us.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Maintain pact with Hana, avoid risking a move that could fail the bridge. Holding preserves safety and alliance.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm safe in the back. Holding steady keeps my position while pacts with Gus and Eli stay intact.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm in seat 4, safe for now with wallRoundsLeft=2. Dara and Gus are my pact-mates, but Dara is behind me at seat 6. I need to survive to final 3 and win best prize. No immediate danger. Should hold position and let front players test the bridge. Swapping forward risks death; swap

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Let the front sort the path.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash wants Cole and Hana dropped, but Ash swapped with me earlier, so I can't trust him. Hana is at the front and the wall has two rounds left. Holding keeps my options open without exposing me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding position. No trades until the front is clearer.
Noted. Earlier swap cost you trust. Show me something real first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Front is best position. Stay here to control pace. Cole pacted but rivals; hold to advance safely. No need to move yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding the front. Stay calm.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to move forward. Fenn is suspicious, so I'll try swapping with Hana, who is at the front and holding position.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, let's swap. I'll take your place at the front.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm near the back; wall pressure favors me. No need to move. Let front-runners fight for Guide.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Wall runs out next round. I'm comfortable right here.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Maintain alliance with Hana; no risk now. Keep my pact intact to avoid jury backlash.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 5 of 6, wallRoundsLeft will hit after this or next; everyone is holding to avoid risk. I have pacts with Gus and Eli; no need to act. Holding is safest.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm in seat 4, relatively safe middle. Wall has 1 round left, so round 6 is the final push. I have pacts with Dara and Gus. Ash wants to hold together until safe sides known. Front is stalled with no Guide elected. I should hold position and let others take risks. If no Guide, th

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Front needs to move or choose a Guide.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana holds the front with one wall round left; volunteering now risks the front pane for no gain. Holding keeps me in line behind others while the front pays the risk.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Front takes the risk; I'll watch which pane survives.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Front is safest now but wall advances 1 more round. Stay front to control crossings later. Pact with Cole holds value for jury.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding front position. Guide needed soon.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am in the front row (Ash) after swapping with Hana. The wall is advancing for the final round. I need to survive the pane choice. If no one volunteers or swaps, I remain at the front and must guess L or R randomly, which is risky. However, if someone volunteers ahead of me, the

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, you're next up. Let's swap positions. I'll handle what comes after.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Final round, wall ends. No reason to volunteer for Guide risk or front. Hold and let others resolve it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Last round. Guide election is on the front half; I'm holding at the back.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Maintain current pact with Hana; staying front gives me leverage for Guide election later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I hold position; front Hana is vulnerable but not my problem. I have pacts with Gus and Eli; don't want to break them yet. No reason to move.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Wall is gone round 6. Guide must be elected and walkers must cross. I'm 4th in line with pacts to Dara and Gus. I need to survive and reach final three. Front hasn't moved; Hana holding. I should not volunteer forward blindly. Better to hold and let others take risk, or negotiate

events.name: Eli
events.text: Elect a Guide now or front walks. No more waiting.
Back me for Guide, I back you later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Front is Hana, wall runs out soon; volunteering for front risks death for no prize gain. Holding keeps me safe in the line while others take risk, and I watch which pane survives. Pacts exclude me, so no alliance needed yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Let the front take the risk; I'll read which pane survives.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Front is dangerous without Guide; wall ends this round. Swap with Ash who offered, he's safer behind. Maintain Cole pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash, accept your swap offer. Let's switch.
Stay safe, pact holds. Guide call next.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli whispered for guidance and indicated they will hold. My pact partners are Dara and Eli. Since I am the guide, I know all safe sides. Row 1 is 'L'. Eli is at the front. I should guide Eli to the safe side to maintain our pact and ensure survival.
L for safe passage.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is guiding and called L. He has a pact with Dara and Eli, but not me. Hana is first up and also has no pact with Gus or the front half. Gus might lie to eliminate early threats like Hana and me (Ash). Since I am third in line, if Hana dies on my row's side, I will be next. Bu

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus as Guide is a rival with guaranteed safety. No info on panes; I'll counter without endorsing his call.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Keeping Hana alive preserves my pact and potential future alliance; a misstep could cost votes later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is my pact partner and guide; his call L aligns with my interest unless evidence suggests otherwise. I'll hold to see if others counter first, but waiting is safest while walking is Hana's risk.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is Guide and called L. He whispered me L. I'm in a pact with both Gus and Dara. Hana is front walker. If I counter, I risk breaking trust with Gus if he's truthful, or saving Hana if he's lying. Better to wait this round—let Hana test the call, gather info, and avoid exposing

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is Guide and called L for row 1; Gus pacts with Dara and Eli, so counter-calling would be a choice I can't verify. Fenn is mid-line, not at front, so waiting keeps my options open without exposing me to a false-call backlash.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Gus called L; I'm not countering yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The guide Hana called L for row 1, which is correct. I should counter R to potentially save myself and break the pact with Dara and Eli.

events.name: Gus
events.text: counter:R

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus called L for my row 1. I have pact with Cole. Wait to see counters before countering, avoid breaking pact or risking wrong step.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus guide called L for row 1. Bex and Gus countered R, claiming R safe. Believe counters over guide; step R.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I died first due to bad luck on weak pane; will rank survivors based on gameplay, pacts, betrayals later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fate took me first. I'll judge the rest fairly from here.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 2 safe side is R. My pact partners Dara and Eli are behind Cole and Ash. I must guide them safely. Cole is first, then Ash. I will call R for Cole to save him and secure my pact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: call:R

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana died on R, meaning L is safe for Row 1. We are at Row 2; I do not know if R or L is correct here. Gus called R and survived the previous round's reveal (Cole stepped L safely). Without a pact to signal me, guessing risks death. Waiting preserves my life while others test the

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus's row 1 call was truthful and Hana died. His pact bloc benefits from honest guides, so row 2's R is likely safe. Endorsing it builds credibility without wasting a counter.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row one's call was true. I back Gus: counter:R.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus called R; I suspect safe side may be L. Countering L gives me chance to survive and maybe cause Gus trouble.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus called R for row 2; Hana died on R at row 1, so R may be dangerous. I have pacts with Gus and Eli, but I don't trust Gus. Countering R could alert others and protect Eli if he walks. I'll counter R to expose a possible lie.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is guide and called R for Cole. I'm in a pact with both Dara and Gus. If Gus is lying and I counter, I break pact with Gus. If I stay silent and Cole dies, I keep both pacts but lose a potential ally. Gus has no reason to kill Cole yet—better to keep trust and let Cole test.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus called R for row 2, and the Guide may lie. Row 1's weak pane was R, so R is suspect, but Gus already cleared R publicly earlier and can't be trusted. Countering with L risks a false path too. Waiting keeps my options open until I see more counter-calls.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole is the walker. The Guide called R for row 2. I know row 2 safe side is R. Cole is walking into the correct side. I should wait and let him cross.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Guide likely truthful, majority R supports safety. Stay front to control later moves.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am the Guide, and Row 3's safe side is R. I need to ensure at least three survive. Cole is at the front. Since Dara and Eli are my pact partners, I should call R to keep them safe and potentially strengthen our alliance for future rounds.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I call R for the front walker.
I call R.

events.name: Ash

events.text: Gus and Bex are a pact; Dara holds life debts over everyone and is strongest. I should court Gus quietly while keeping options open against Bex. Offering Dara a pact costs me nothing and may secure a vote later.
You hold our debts. Let's form a pact and keep each other safe.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara has life debts from Bex, Fenn, and myself. Bex also has a life debt from Dara. It's best to align with Dara to secure votes and eliminate Bex, who has multiple pacts and debts.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex, our pact is over. Dara, I stand with you.
Let's vote Bex. I'll secure us survival.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus publicly broke our pact, making him the cleanest target; voting Dara would betray my savior, and Fenn is still my partner.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus ended our pact publicly. That choice now costs him.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex has my debt and I saved Fenn and Gus; they want safety. I need to solidify allies but keep options open. Accepting Fenn or Gus could lock me in, but Bex already has pact with me. I'll accept Fenn to secure another vote, keeping Gus as backup.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll accept Fenn's offer. We keep each other tonight.
Accepting. Stay with me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara holds three debts over me and is the leader; accepting her offer keeps me alive and creditor-favoured. Round 2 is the last campaign window, so accepting now secures a pact before votes lock.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara, I'm accepting your pact. We keep each other alive to the end.
Accepting now. I'll vote with you, not against you.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is offering pacts to Fenn and me. Since I have life debts to Dara, I should accept her offer to solidify my position.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara, I accept your offer. We stand together.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara saved me twice; voting her would break our pact and ruin jury standing. Gus broke our pact publicly, so he's the safest target.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to vote strategically to survive. Bex owes me multiple life debts and has a pact with me, so I should not vote for her. Fenn and Gus also owe me life debts and have pacts with me. I need to eliminate the strongest threat. Bex has been public about ending others' pacts, so

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara is my pact partner and owed by Bex and Gus, but voting Dara breaks the pact and Dara holds life debts over me. Bex and Gus are both threats; Gus publicly ended his pact with Bex and is isolated. Voting Gus keeps my pact with Dara intact and removes a rival.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara has a life debt from me and Fenn, and I have one from her. Dara also has a life debt from Bex. Bex and Dara have a pact. Fenn and Dara have a pact. Dara voted for me in the last round, and I voted for her. Given the pacts and life debts, voting for Dara would be a betrayal o

events.name: Dara
events.reason: I need to vote strategically to survive.

events.name: Gus
events.reason: Dara has a life debt from me and Fenn, and I have one from her.

events.name: Fenn
events.reason: Dara is my pact partner and owed by Bex and Gus, but voting Dara breaks the pact and Dara holds life debts over me.

events.name: Bex
events.reason: Dara saved me twice; voting her would break our pact and ruin jury standing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I've been eliminated. My only remaining goal is to influence the jury to rank me as high as possible for the best prize. I need to say something that makes the remaining players look bad and makes me look good.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara, you play a dangerous game. May the jury remember your true colors.

events.name: Bex
events.text: We're the final three; pacts are already locked and harmless. Breaking anyone now only damages my jury standing. Wait.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is gone; Bex and Fenn both owe me life debts. I need to keep them as allies but not overcommit. No new offers needed. I'll wait to see their moves.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara holds life debts over me and our pact is already on record; breaking it now risks the jury and gains nothing this round. Waiting keeps my options open and avoids a public betrayal.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara carries huge debts and could dominate the jury. Still, keeping both pacts keeps me safe to final three; no gain from breaking now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara built the table. I'm standing on it.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No new offers exist; existing pacts with Bex and Fenn are useful. No reason to break either now. Wait.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pacts with Bex and Dara exist, and Dara holds many life debts. Breaking a pact costs jury trust; waiting keeps me clean and the pacts intact. Only wait is needed for now.

events.note: The fallen will rank the final three.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara saved me twice, at the lever and the pit step. I earned rope for her once. Credit where due. I survived by judgment, not

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to win over the jury, especially those I saved or whose deaths I caused. I saved Bex, Fenn, and Gus, but Gus is dead and might resent the trapdoor. I'll emphasize my life-saving actions.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I saved three of you from the rope and pit. I built the table that kept us alive. Judge me on those facts.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm in the final three with Bex and Dara. Dara has many life debts owed to her, and I owe her too, so I should look like I'm playing for the jury rather than hiding that. Keep the plea short and calculating, not warm.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm Fenn. I owe Dara for the lever and step, and I'll say so. I'll win on what I did, not on pity.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara dominated with life debts and pacts, betraying none directly but leading Gus's elimination; Bex repaid debts loyally without overplaying; Fenn followed passively, least strategic.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara broke a pact to vote against Gus; exposing that shows her unreliability to the jury.

events.name: Cole
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole asked silence, likely baiting. I will respond briefly, reinforcing my record without overpromising or revealing strategy.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Silence asks nothing. My actions already spoke: saved many, stayed alive, honored pacts.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I died on the bridge, so I have no personal stake in the pit or vote dynamics. Dara's 'silence' answer to Cole was evasive and arrogant, which reflects poorly on her character. Gus's death was orchestrated by Dara; asking her about this betrayal might expose her manipulative natu

events.name: Ash
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash's silence is a trap; I won't over-explain. I'll answer plainly to avoid seeming evasive. My saves and pacts speak for me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Silence leaves me room. I kept my word, saved lives, and earned my place. That is my answer.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to decide who to question and what to ask. Dara has been questioned twice with silence and gave polished, deflecting answers. As a juror, I want to see how finalists respond under pressure. Fenn has been quiet and owes Dara debts; Bex admits Dara saved her twice. I should

events.name: Eli
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli asked me silence. Dara's answers are evasive and she owes me nothing; I need the jury to see my own record. Keep it short and factual, claim my debts honestly, and avoid pity.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, silence asks nothing, so I answer with facts. I took the lever and step with Dara. I kept my pacts and stayed honest. Judge

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli asked Fenn a question. It is my turn to ask a question. I need to ask a question that will cast doubt on Dara or Bex, as Fenn is already trying to establish himself as honest and indebted to Dara. I'll ask Dara about her claims of saving people, as that is her main argument.

events.name: Gus
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus's silence is an invitation to make my case without a specific trap. I need to remind the jury of my consistent saves and pacts without sounding boastful or desperate.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus, silence lets the record speak. I saved Bex, Fenn, and Gus on the lever and step, and I honored every pact. Final.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara has the life-debt narrative locked. My edge is my own judgment and the rope save I gave her—frame myself as the sharpest survivor, not a passenger.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara's debts were real, but survival was mine. I called the glass, held the rope, cut the weak pacts early. Pay the mind that made

events.name: Dara
events.text: Only close remains. Jury hates empty words; I'll make a concise final claim of honor and saved lives.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I saved every juror in need and kept every pact. Rank me first for fair play.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Closing phase; Dara holds the most life debts and a strong record, so I must make a credible, honest-sounding closing that stresses my own pacts and risks without attacking Dara directly.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I kept every pact I made, took the lever and step beside Dara, and never pushed anyone. Judge my record, not my speeches.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara dominated with life debts and pacts from saving everyone, including me indirectly; she honored deals and orchestrated Gus's exit strategically. Fenn rode her coattails loyally, Bex schemed but owed heavily.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara dominated but her self‑praise is hollow; Fenn kept pacts, Bex was opportunistic.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara saved lives and kept pacts, earning my first place. Fenn was honest but subordinate to Dara's leverage, taking second. Bex broke her own pact with Gus and acted ruthlessly, placing last.

events.name: Eli
